chunks: What the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Basir,
he [Abu Basir] said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): '[Regarding] the madhiy that comes out of a man —'

He [the Imam] said: 'Shall I set for you a rule (hadd) regarding it?' He [Abu Basir] said: I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said, then said: 'If it comes from you with desire (shahwa), then perform wudu. And if it comes from you otherwise, there is no wudu upon you for it.'

key_terms.اَلْمَذْيُ: madhiy — pre-seminal fluid; the bodily discharge whose ritual-legal status is determined here
key_terms.حَدّاً: hadd — a defined legal rule or criterion set by the Imam
key_terms.شَهْوَةٍ: shahwa — sexual desire or arousal; the determining criterion for wudu obligation
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat

ai.seo_question: Does pre-seminal fluid (madhiy) require wudu in Shia Islam, and what criterion did Imam al-Sadiq establish for its ruling?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about the legal ruling on madhiy (pre-seminal fluid) discharged by a man. The Imam established a precise criterion: if madhiy exits with sexual desire (shahwa), wudu becomes obligatory; if it exits without desire, no wudu is required. This is a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh on ritual purity, distinguishing the legal status of madhiy from that of maniy (semen), which necessitates ghusl.
